# The NVIC: priorities, preemption, latency: the exercise

<!-- Generated by tools/maintainer/build_exercise_readmes.py from the lesson page. Edit the lesson, then run the script. -->

Lesson: [The NVIC: priorities, preemption, latency](https://jouhis.github.io/embedded-course/lessons/0072-the-nvic.html). Read it first: the steps below refer to its diagrams and worked examples.

## Try it in Wokwi

The button on PB0 raises EXTI0, PB0 being routed to EXTI line 0 through the AFIO external-interrupt register (`AFIO->EXTICR[0]`, which the solution sets to the PB value, `AFIO_EXTICR1_EXTI0_PB`), with the pin on the default mapping of the [STM32F103x8/xB datasheet, "Pinouts and pin description" table](https://www.st.com/resource/en/datasheet/stm32f103c8.pdf). The EXTI0 handler is slow, busy-waiting for about 30 ms at priority 2, while a timer on TIM2 raises an update interrupt every 10 ms at priority 0, and the log records every event with a sequence number, so the order shows on the serial monitor.

1. Open `projects/0072-the-nvic/starter` in VS Code, build with <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>B</kbd> and start the simulator with <kbd>F1</kbd> → *Wokwi: Start Simulator*.
2. In `nvic_start()`, set the grouping to 3 and give TIM2 priority 0 and EXTI0 priority 2 with `NVIC_EncodePriority`, then press the button.
3. The program works when the serial monitor shows `TIM2 nested in EXTI0` between the `EXTI0 enter` and `EXTI0 exit` lines, whereas before the fix the starter shows only `TIM2 tick` lines after the EXTI0 exit.

Look at the order in `tim2_tick_start()`: the update interrupt (`DIER.UIE`) is enabled only after the `EGR` write and the flag clear. The `UG` write sets the update flag, so with the interrupt already on it would raise a tick that never happened. In Wokwi it is worse: an interrupt raised by a store returns to that store and runs it again, so the program would hang before its first line. Also, Wokwi reads both priorities back as 0 in the startup line, even though the nesting shows they are set.
